memories.content: HCI reviewers find it difficult to assess the reproducibility of results if the prototype version used in the evaluation is not disclosed.
Record the manipulated and fixed elements of compared design alternatives so that other researchers can reconstruct them.
Records of formative evaluation decisions enable the reconstruction of connections between raw data, interpretation, and design modifications.
The user must make it possible to trace which observations each prototype version reflects so the process of deriving design knowledge can be reviewed.
List whom to notify and in what order if serious discomfort is reported during the study.
Field staff rely on the pre-defined contact sequence when serious discomfort is reported.
Define the thresholds for participant harm, operational disruption, and data anomalies at which deployment and data collection must cease.
Establish procedures to restore existing systems and workflow states after suspending field deployment.
The user's stop plan can be judged feasible only when it identifies who has authority to order recovery and who is responsible for carrying it out.

In organizations where error reporting is linked to individual performance evaluations, safety signal records may be separated from research decision logs, potentially breaking the traceability path for the same incident.

analysis.overview: The frames address complementary governance needs: the reference emphasizes reproducible design provenance, while the compared frame emphasizes field-safety escalation, stopping, and recovery. Their only substantive intersection is traceability, with an organizational condition that can disrupt links between incident evidence and research decisions.

relations.reason: The reference memories establish evidence-to-design provenance across formative decisions and prototype versions; the compared memory adds an explicit organizational condition under which that provenance path may be broken.
relations.summary: Research evidence should remain traceable through interpretation and design changes, but performance-linked error reporting can cause safety records for an incident to be separated from the relevant decision history.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful reproducibility requirement found only in the reference frame.
relations.summary: The evaluated prototype version should be disclosed so reviewers can assess reproducibility.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful documentation requirement found only in the reference frame.
relations.summary: Manipulated and fixed elements of compared design alternatives should be recorded to permit reconstruction.

relations.reason: The compared memories state complementary parts of one operational escalation rule found only in that frame.
relations.summary: A predefined notification sequence should identify whom field staff contact, and in what order, after serious discomfort is reported.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful stopping-policy requirement found only in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Thresholds for participant harm, operational disruption, and data anomalies should determine when deployment and data collection cease.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful recovery-procedure requirement found only in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Procedures should restore existing systems and workflow states after field deployment is suspended.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful recovery-governance requirement found only in the compared frame.
relations.summary: A feasible stop plan should identify who may order recovery and who must execute it.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame uniquely specifies discomfort escalation, cessation thresholds, restoration procedures, and recovery authority and responsibility.
reports.differences: Both address traceable evidence-to-decision paths, while performance-linked error reporting may cause safety records to be separated and break that traceability.
reports.reference_only: The reference uniquely requires disclosure of evaluated prototype versions and documentation of controlled differences between design alternatives.
